title: Consumption of one egg per day increases serum lutein and zeaxanthin concentrations in older adults without altering serum lipid and lipoprotein cholesterol concentrations
authors: Goodrow EF, Wilson TA, Houde SC, Vishwanathan R, Scollin PA, Handelman G, et al.
followUp: 18 weeks: 4-week run-in, two 5-week interventions separated by a 4-week washout
population: Adults aged 60 to 96 years (mean 79), 22 from nursing homes and 11 from senior centres and a university, taking neither lutein supplements nor lipid-lowering drugs
funder: Supported by the American Egg Board, Egg Nutrition Center, Washington, DC (R.J.N.) and the Massachusetts Lions Eye Research Fund, New Bedford, MA (R.J.N.).
inKindSupport: Eggs for cholesterol analysis were provided by the nursing homes or donated by the Aramark Corporation; lutein and zeaxanthin standards were provided by Hoffman-La Roche.
result: Randomised crossover of 1 egg per day against no egg or egg substitute, 5 weeks each. Serum lutein rose by 26% and zeaxanthin by 38% after 5 weeks of 1 egg per day compared with the phase before eggs (P < 0.001). Serum total, LDL and HDL cholesterol and triglycerides did not differ between egg and no-egg phases; the mean increases in total and LDL cholesterol were 0.6% and 3.2%. Sampled yolks contained 210 ± 9 mg cholesterol, 143 ± 28 µg lutein and 94 ± 18 µg zeaxanthin.
